'''Sykes Enterprises, Inc.''' (stylized as '''SYKES''') was an American [[multinational corporation|multinational]] [[business process outsourcing]] provider headquartered in [[Tampa, Florida]]. The company provided business process outsourcing (BPO) services, IT consulting, and IT-enabled services, such as [[technical support]] and [[customer service]].

In 2021, [[Sitel Group]] acquired Sykes for $2.2 billion.<ref name="bizjournals.com 2021">{{cite web | website=bizjournals.com | date=August 31, 2021 | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/southflorida/news/2021/08/31/sykes-2-billion-sale-officially-closes.html | access-date=March 7, 2023|title=Sykes goes private with Miami group's $2.2 billion all-cash deal}}</ref> In March 2023, Sitel and Sykes fully merged to form [[Foundever]].

==History==
Sykes was founded in 1977 by [[John H. Sykes]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], to provide engineering and design services to large corporations.<ref>{{cite news |title=Volunteering Left and Right |first=Steve |last=Cranford |newspaper=[[Charlotte Business Journal|The Business Journal Serving Charlotte and the Metropolitan Area]] |date=November 19, 1990 |page=14}}</ref> Companies such as [[IBM]], [[AT&T]], and [[Texas Instruments]] were among Sykes' first clients. 

In 1992, the company moved into the [[customer service]] business by purchasing Jones Technologies, a [[call center]] company based in [[Sterling, Colorado]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.journal-advocate.com/2013/04/05/call-center-operations-thriving-after-2-decades/ |location=[[Sterling, Colorado]] |newspaper=[[Journal-Advocate]] |first=David |last=Martinez |title=Call Center Operations Thriving After 2 Decades |date=April 6, 2013 |access-date=June 12, 2016}}</ref>

In 1993, Sykes relocated its corporate headquarters from Charlotte to [[Tampa, Florida]].<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[St. Petersburg Times]] |title=Computer Company to Move to Tampa |date=August 11, 1993 |first=Alan |last=Goldstein |page=1E}}</ref>

Sykes became a publicly traded company in 1996.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |agency=[[Bloomberg Business News]] |access-date=June 11, 2016 |date=May 1, 1996 |title=Shares of Sykes Enterprises Nearly Double on Day One |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/05/01/business/company-news-shares-of-sykes-enterprises-nearly-double-on-day-one.html}}</ref> The company was listed on [[NASDAQ]] under the stock symbol SYKE.

David Grimes, a former AT&T executive, was named president of Sykes in 1998.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=St. Petersburg Times |first=Scott |last=Barancik |title=Sykes hands chief executive post to protege |url=http://www.sptimes.com/News/072800/Business/Sykes_hands_chief_exe.shtml |date=July 28, 2000 |access-date=June 18, 2016}}</ref> John Sykes remained CEO and chairman. In 2000, Grimes became president and CEO. However, after 3 months, Grimes resigned and Sykes returned as president and CEO.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[Tampa Bay Business Journal]] |title=John Sykes to head Sykes Enterprises, again |url=http://www.bizjournals.com/tampabay/stories/2000/11/13/daily4.html |date=November 13, 2000 |access-date=June 18, 2016}}</ref>

Charles Sykes, John Sykes' son, became president and CEO of the company in 2004.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=St. Petersburg Times |first=Kris |last=Hundley |title=Founder of Sykes Retires - Again |url=http://www.sptimes.com/2004/08/03/Business/Founder_of_Sykes_reti.shtml |date=August 3, 2004 |access-date=June 17, 2016}}</ref> Charles had been with the company 17 years before assuming his father's position.

On June 18, 2021, a [[Sitel Group]] subsidiary acquired all outstanding shares of Sykes in a cash transaction valued at approximately $2.2 billion, removing the company from Nasdaq's publicly traded companies. The Sitel Group, in its new combination, brings together 160,000 employees in 40 countries, serving more than 700 customers and in more than 50 languages.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Sitel Group® Completes Acquisition of Sykes Enterprises, Inc. |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sitel-group-completes-acquisition-of-sykes-enterprises-inc-301368494.html |access-date=2021-12-11 |website=[[PR Newswire]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Acquisitions ===
In 1992, Sykes purchased Jones Technologies, Inc. in [[Sterling, Colorado]] and entered into the [[customer support]] business.<ref name="CRM">{{Cite web |date=2013-06-08 |title=CRM Review – Sykes Contact Center Services |url=https://sellmorenow.com/crm-review/sykes-enterprises/ |access-date=2021-12-11 |website=SellMoreNow |language=en-US}}</ref> Four years later, Sykes acquired Datasvar Support AB of Sweden and Diagsoft Inc. of [[Scotts Valley, California]];<ref>{{Cite news |date=1996-09-03 |title=Short: Sykes bought Diagsoft |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/short-sykes-bought-diagsoft/ |access-date=2021-12-07 |website=[[CNET]] |language=en}}</ref> one year after this, they purchased bothMcQueen International Limited and the German company Telcare. In 2006, Sykes acquired [[Argentina]]-based Apex America; in 2010, they acquired [[ICT Group]].<ref name="CRM" /> In 2012, Sykes purchased Alpine Access<ref>{{cite web |last=Stevenson |first=Chelsea |title=Sykes Enterprises to buy Alpine Access for $150M |url=http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sykes-enterprises-to-buy-alpine-access-for-150m-2012-07-30 |website=[[MarketWatch]] |date=30 July 2012 |access-date=30 July 2012}}</ref> and three years later a company called Qelp. In 2016, Sykes acquired Clearlink from Utah<ref>{{Cite news |title=Sykes buys fast growing Utah firm |url=http://www.bizjournals.com/tampabay/blog/morning-edition/2016/03/sykes-buys-fast-growing-utah-firm.html |access-date=2017-02-08 |newspaper=[[Tampa Bay Business Journal]]}}</ref> and two years later the [[Robotic process automation]] service provider Symphony Ventures.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=October 22, 2018 |title=Sykes Enterprises, Incorporated Acquires Pure-Play & Best-of-Breed RPA Service Provider Symphony Ventures Limited |work=[[GlobeNewswire]] |url=https://globenewswire.com/news-release/2018/10/22/1625027/0/en/Sykes-Enterprises-Incorporated-Acquires-Pure-Play-Best-of-Breed-RPA-Service-Provider-Symphony-Ventures-Limited.html |access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> In 2020, Sykes carried out its last acquisition before being acquired by the Sitel Group in 2021. It purchased Taylor Media Corp. (TMC), a personal finance digital media company and owner of The Penny Hoarder.<ref>{{Cite press release |publisher=Sykes Enterprises, Inc. |date=2020-12-21|title=Sykes Enterprises, Incorporated, Through Its Clearlink Subsidiary, Acquires Personal Finance Digital Media Company the Penny Hoarder |url=https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2020/12/21/2148584/7267/en/Sykes-Enterprises-Incorporated-Through-Its-Clearlink-Subsidiary-Acquires-Personal-Finance-Digital-Media-Company-the-Penny-Hoarder.html |access-date=2021-12-07 |website=[[GlobeNewswire]] |language=en}}</ref>

Sykes Enterprises, Inc. (stylized as SYKES) was an American multinational business process outsourcing provider headquartered in Tampa, Florida. The company provided business process outsourcing (BPO) services, IT consulting, and IT-enabled services, such as technical support and customer service.
In 2021, Sitel Group acquired Sykes for $2.2 billion. In March 2023, Sitel and Sykes fully merged to form Foundever.
